projects.name: PCXPay
projects.role: Senior Software Engineer — Backend, Payments & DevOps
projects.tagline: Cross-border payments infrastructure: one API across stablecoin, Lightning and traditional banking rails.
projects.problem: Businesses moving money across borders lose 3–5% to correspondent banks and wait days for settlement. Building compliant multi-country payment rails in-house takes years of banking partnerships, and every partner brings its own failure modes: duplicate webhooks, partial settlements, and reconciliation gaps that regulators notice.
projects.solution: Spearheaded backend, payments and DevOps work on the platform. Integrated the GTBank Squad gateway end to end, from technical scoping with the bank's engineers through production cutover, owning reconciliation, idempotency and gateway-specific error handling. Built and shipped AWS Lambda payment services in Python across UK, Nigerian and Canadian banking rails, and instrumented the whole fleet with Sentry distributed tracing.
projects.system: Event-driven microservices on AWS (Lambda, API Gateway, ECS) with Terraform-managed infrastructure and CloudHSM-backed key custody. Webhook-driven reconciliation flips transaction state on gateway callbacks and flags mismatches automatically. Live settlement runs across multiple banking partners under FCA oversight. The platform later spun out as an independent FCA-regulated money transfer operator.
projects.dsa: Idempotency keys with TTL windows and Bloom-filter deduplication make repeated webhook deliveries safe: the same callback processed twice produces one ledger effect. Reconciliation is a state machine, so every transaction is in exactly one auditable state.
projects.why: Python on Lambda keeps each payment concern small, independently deployable and cheap at idle; Terraform makes every environment reproducible; Sentry tracing across services turns a cross-border failure into a single followable trail instead of five log searches.
projects.innovation: Treating the bank gateway as an unreliable narrator: every inbound event is verified, deduplicated and reconciled against internal state before money moves, which is what lets the platform operate under FCA scrutiny.
metrics: GTBank Squad integrated from scoping to production cutover
Settlement rails live across UK, Nigerian and Canadian banking partners
Sentry distributed tracing across the whole service fleet
Terraform-provisioned AWS with CloudHSM key custody
Platform spun out as an independent FCA-regulated money transfer operator
projects.potential: Embedded finance for platforms that need global payouts without building banking partnerships themselves.
projects.note: Senior Software Engineer spearheading backend, payments integrations and cloud infrastructure on a 15–30 person, four-country engineering team.

projects.name: Dwelix
projects.tagline: A safer way to rent property: verified listings, controlled access and legally backed agreements.
projects.problem: Renting in emerging markets means agent extortion, fabricated listings, spoofed locations and paper leases nobody can audit. A trusted marketplace needs ground-truth verification, controlled physical access to properties, and money that moves only when the legal steps have actually happened.
projects.solution: Led the engineering team and built the platform: 12 Go microservices behind an API gateway covering auth, marketplace, property, search, geo, payments, legal agreements, uploads, referrals, users and blog. Scouts physically verify every property; keys stay in Dwelix custody with every entry logged; lawyers verify ownership and agreements are e-signed through Documenso; rent and deposits move through audited escrow.
projects.system: 12 Go (Fiber) services, each independently containerised on GCP Cloud Run, talking gRPC with GCP Pub/Sub event streams for state transitions. 137 versioned PostgreSQL migrations, Redis caching, Cloudflare at the edge, Terraform-provisioned dev/staging/production, Cloud Build CI/CD and Sentry observability. A React + TypeScript frontend of 127 pages and 376 components serves role-based dashboards for tenants, landlords, scouts, agents, lawyers and admins.
projects.dsa: Geospatial bounding-box indexing flags coordinates that don't match a claimed address. Lease execution runs inside atomic database transactions paired with cryptographic document hashing, so a signed agreement and its escrow state can never disagree. Paystack callbacks drive a webhook reconciliation flow that flags mismatches automatically.
projects.why: Go and Fiber give small memory footprints and predictable latency during search spikes; gRPC keeps service contracts typed; Pub/Sub decouples property state changes from everything that reacts to them; Cloud Run lets each service scale to zero independently.
projects.innovation: Joining the physical and legal worlds in one pipeline: ground scouts, custodied keys, lawyer-verified ownership and e-signed leases feed an escrow that only releases when each real-world step is recorded.
metrics: 12 Go microservices plus an API gateway, gRPC + Pub/Sub
100,000+ lines of Go across 300+ files
137 versioned PostgreSQL migrations
127 frontend pages and 376 components across role-based dashboards
Documenso e-signed agreements with audited escrow
Terraform-provisioned GCP across dev, staging and production
projects.potential: A standard for secure tenancy across African cities and a safe rental channel for diaspora property owners.

projects.name: Mopcare

projects.problem: Elderly care programmes run on spreadsheets and WhatsApp groups: no reliable way to dispatch caregivers, certify volunteers, or give diaspora families visibility into how a parent is doing.
projects.solution: Direct backend development and technical leadership on a digital health platform serving close to 2,000 elderly patients. Owns the Go microservices, the volunteer management system with automated certificate generation, the accredited healthcare LMS, and the React portals for clients, caregivers and institutions. Migrated legacy services from Rust to Go for maintainability, and mentors the engineers on the team.

Role-based access control isolates health data per role. React + TypeScript portals (Zustand, TanStack Query, Tailwind, shadcn/ui). Terraform-provisioned AWS, Docker, and CI/CD through GitHub Actions.
projects.dsa: Stateful task scheduling assigns caregivers with conflict resolution so one person is never double-booked. Certificates are generated with verifiable identifiers so a volunteer's accreditation can be checked by anyone.
projects.why: Go for a small, predictable backend that a small team can maintain, which is why the earlier Rust services were migrated; Redis for the low-latency notification path; RBAC because health data must be isolated per role by construction.

projects.name: Scholelabs
projects.tagline: Run an entire school from one platform: grading, enrolment, staff and communication.
projects.problem: Schools across Nigeria run on fragmented spreadsheets and handwritten logs: slow, insecure and error-prone. A shared platform must serve many schools at once without any school ever seeing another's data.
projects.solution: Owned the backend of a multi-tenant school management platform through to launch. Wrote the REST APIs and domain services behind student grading, bulk enrolment, performance data and staff portal management, and enforced role-based access control across administrators, staff and student records.
projects.system: TypeScript on NestJS with Fastify, Sequelize over PostgreSQL, BullMQ workers on Redis for bulk operations, Resend for email, and Sentry telemetry. Tenant-scoping middleware isolates every institution's data. Deployed continuously on Railway.

projects.why: NestJS gives enforceable module boundaries for a growing domain; Fastify keeps request overhead low; BullMQ moves slow bulk work off the request path so grading stays responsive.
projects.innovation: Onboarding a whole school in days: bulk enrolment, role-based portals and CRM messaging arrive as one product instead of a stack of tools.

projects.name: Topnorch
projects.tagline: One tap, application sent. AI job matching that tailors every resume and cover letter.
projects.problem: Job hunting is repetitive: read a posting, rewrite a resume, rewrite a cover letter, repeat dozens of times. Blind auto-apply tools spam employers and damage the candidate's reputation.
projects.solution: Built a polyglot backend: a Rust parser for deep PDF resume extraction, Python NLP pipelines that tailor each resume and cover letter to a role, and Go orchestration services managing job dispatch queues, behind a React + TypeScript interface. A human stays in the loop: nothing is sent until the candidate taps apply.
projects.system: Modular monolith combining compiled Rust utilities, Python inference pipelines and Go orchestration daemons. PostgreSQL with Prisma for candidate profiles, Redis caching, distributed rate limiting to protect candidate accounts across job boards, and Sentry telemetry.
projects.dsa: Skill graphs from resumes are matched against parsed job descriptions with vector similarity. Token-bucket rate limiters, shared across workers, keep applications within each board's limits.
projects.why: Rust where parsing speed matters, Python where the NLP ecosystem lives, Go where concurrency and queues matter: each language sits where its strength is.
projects.innovation: Human-in-the-loop automation: the system does the tedious tailoring and matching, and the candidate keeps the final decision.

Distributed rate limiting across global job boards
AI resume and cover-letter tailoring per posting

projects.solution: Developed the frontend architecture and built an automated FFmpeg video processing pipeline that renders, scales, and compresses 4K beauty reels into optimized web formats, distributed globally through Cloudflare R2 object storage.

projects.why: Go Fiber provides sub-millisecond throughput for high-volume vote casting; Signal Protocol delivers mathematical zero-knowledge privacy guarantees directly in the browser.
projects.innovation: Self-healing cryptographic voting architecture where ballot corruption is mathematically impossible and production incidents trigger automated diagnostic and repair runs.

projects.name: Akin
projects.tagline: Keeps students in class when they cannot afford the commute.
projects.problem: In a large cohort, attendance is bimodal. Some students quietly drop out because the daily trip costs more than they have, and the gap stays invisible until someone has already stopped showing up. A public donation board humiliates. Ad-hoc cash never reconciles. Just carpool has no safety net.
projects.solution: Two coordinated rails over one shared identity and an audited ledger: a pooled cash Transport Fund that givers contribute to through Paystack, and an in-kind ride network. The metric it optimises for is retention with dignity, not money raised.
projects.system: A Fiber HTTP and WebSocket API, GORM over Postgres, Redis for sessions and cache, Svix for webhooks, Resend for email, goose migrations, role-aware flows, and a full audit trail. A Vite, React and TypeScript PWA fronts it for low-end and offline-prone campus phones.
projects.dsa: The wallet ledger uses pessimistic row locking (GORM clause.Locking strength UPDATE, a SELECT FOR UPDATE) so two concurrent disbursements can never double-spend the fund. Worker pools coordinate the two rails in real time.
projects.why: Go and Fiber for concurrent coordination of two rails plus live WebSocket updates. A React PWA because the people who need this are on cheap phones and flaky networks, and the app has to load anyway.
projects.innovation: Dignity is encoded into the architecture, not bolted on. A cash rail and an in-kind rail reconcile inside one ledger, so help looks like a quiet transaction rather than a charity feed with someone's name on it.
metrics: zero double-spend via locked-ledger disbursement
real-time ride coordination over WebSocket
designed for a 500-person cohort, scales to a campus

projects.potential: Campus-wide rollouts, NGO and CSR-funded programs, and any community where transport cost is a silent dropout driver.

projects.name: Corvus
projects.problem: nmap, masscan and rustscan answer one question, what is open right now, then throw the state away. In security the signal that matters is the change: what appeared, what vanished, when, and why.
projects.solution: A stateful network intelligence engine. Corvus versions every host, port and service observation as a time series, diffs each scan against history, fuses passive intelligence before scanning, surfaces anomalies, correlates CVEs, and answers questions in plain English. Solo-built full-stack: 10.7k lines of Go across 24 packages plus a 7.6k-line Next.js dashboard.
projects.system: One Go binary exposes a CLI, a Bubble Tea TUI, and a Fiber REST API with WebSocket streaming. Observations persist in an embedded bbolt store. Nodes coordinate over an encrypted UDP gossip mesh. The Next.js 16 frontend renders scans, host history, the mesh, and the natural-language ask view.
projects.dsa: Temporal records are keyed by big-endian timestamps, so the store's natural key order is chronological and history range-scans become a single cursor seek. The diff engine is a set reconciliation of ports seen this scan against ports the store believes open, which is how closed ports get detected. Token-bucket rate limiting governs scan rate, and worker pools fan out the scanning.
projects.why: Go gives a single static binary, goroutine-driven concurrency for scanning thousands of endpoints at once, and a first-class network stack. Next.js carries the streaming dashboard.
projects.innovation: Change is a first-class event, not a diff you compute by hand. Predictive intelligence scores a target from DNS, ASN and certificate-transparency data before a single packet is sent, so scanning starts smart instead of brute-forcing 65,535 ports.
metrics: thousands of hosts scanned concurrently per node
sub-second delta detection per scan cycle
horizontal scaling via a leaderless mesh
race-tested CI on every push
projects.potential: Continuous attack-surface monitoring and cloud-drift detection as a product. The temporal core is a moat competitors structurally lack.

projects.name: go-payroll-engine
projects.tagline: Async bulk salary disbursement, built to fintech production standards.
projects.problem: Paying thousands of people at once is a correctness problem, not a CRUD problem. Duplicate payouts, failed retries and compliance are where payroll systems break. And the salary-advance market beside it traps workers in roughly 30 percent interest loans.
projects.solution: An async bulk disbursement engine that batches payouts onto a job queue, dedups aggressively, and treats every payment as idempotent. Compliance with PCI DSS, NDPR, SOC 2 and CBN is designed in from the start rather than retrofitted.
projects.system: A Gin API in front of GORM, Postgres and Redis, with asynq running the disbursement workers off a queue, Prometheus for observability, golang-migrate for schema, and JWT auth. Provider webhooks feed back through deduplicated handlers.
projects.dsa: A Redis-backed Bloom filter gives O(1) duplicate-webhook detection at roughly 1 percent false-positive and zero false-negative. An LRU cache holds per-key rate limiters so each tenant is throttled independently. Idempotency keys in Redis with a 24h TTL make retries safe. asynq provides priority worker queues.
projects.why: Go for high-throughput concurrent disbursement with predictable latency, a mature async-queue ecosystem in asynq, and a strong fintech tooling story.
projects.innovation: Earned-wage access without the debt trap. Instead of a 30 percent loan, an employee draws a slice of pay they have already earned, accrued daily from verified work. Three guardrails keep it healthy: a tapering access curve that shrinks the available percentage as payday nears, an automatic micro-savings skim that locks a small cut of every advance into savings, and a financial-health score that rewards restraint with better terms.
metrics: thousands of payees per batch run
near-zero duplicate payouts via bloom and idempotency
bounded p99 via async queue back-pressure
4.2k lines of Go
projects.potential: Payroll-as-infrastructure for African SMEs, with the earned-wage-access layer as a humane alternative to predatory advances.

projects.name: Bukr
projects.tagline: Cloud-native ticketing where inventory cannot oversell.
projects.problem: Event ticketing fails in two predictable ways. It oversells under burst load when everyone buys at once, and the fee model quietly erodes trust. Both are architecture problems, not bad luck.
projects.solution: A polyglot modular monolith. A Go and Fiber gateway owns auth, events, users and orchestration. A Rust and Axum core owns the correctness and throughput critical path: tickets, the gate scanner, payments and analytics. Supabase and Postgres for data and auth, Redis for cache and sessions.
projects.system: Gateway and core talk over gRPC and HTTP and split by responsibility rather than fashion. Redis caches hot reads and holds sessions. Payment integration, an influencer and affiliate portal, credits, and a QR gate scanner round out the surface. A Vite and React SPA fronts it.
projects.dsa: SELECT FOR UPDATE row locking inside transactions guards invite-token redemption, credit balances and influencer earnings, so two concurrent requests cannot double-redeem or oversell. The system uses heap-based ordering and per-route rate limiting, and the gateway-core split is itself a decision about where correctness must be strongest.
projects.why: Go for the I/O-bound gateway where developer velocity and concurrency win, and Rust for the hot path where memory safety and raw throughput on ticket inventory and payments matter most.
projects.innovation: A dual-language modular monolith that puts the language where it earns its keep, plus an influencer-driven distribution engine and a hybrid smart-pricing fee model designed against local market benchmarks.
metrics: oversell-proof sales under burst via row locks
low-latency gate validation from the Rust core
Redis-cached hot reads and sessions
11k Go plus a Rust core plus a 175-file React frontend
projects.potential: A pan-African ticketing and event platform where reliability under a flash sale is the whole differentiator.

projects.name: Fleetform
projects.tagline: Infrastructure as code with a memory-safe core and a live graph.
projects.problem: IaC planners are powerful but opaque. You apply and hope the ordering is right. And the dominant engines run on a garbage-collected runtime where a state-graph bug becomes a footgun.
projects.solution: A Rust core engine that plans and applies infrastructure with a memory-safe state and dependency model, paired with a Go and Fiber web dashboard that streams plan progress and renders the dependency graph in real time. HCL config, a module system, and multi-backend state across file, S3 and Consul.
projects.system: The Rust core owns parsing, the resource graph and apply. The Go and Fiber layer serves the dashboard and pushes live updates over WebSocket. Proto definitions bridge the two.
projects.dsa: The heart of the planner is a resource dependency DAG with topological sort via petgraph toposort and cycle detection, so apply order is provably correct and cycles fail loudly instead of corrupting state.
projects.why: Rust for the safety-critical graph and state engine where a bug means broken infrastructure, and Go with Fiber for the real-time web layer where iteration speed matters.
projects.innovation: A live dependency-graph dashboard over a compiled, memory-safe core. An IaC tool that shows you the shape of your infrastructure as it plans.
metrics: deterministic plan ordering via toposort
compiled-core speed over interpreted planners
multi-backend state across file, S3 and Consul
projects.potential: An open-source IaC alternative for teams that want safety and visibility, not just parity.
projects.note: Early-stage. Rust core plus Go UI.
